conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of lung
conditions.note: Non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe.

reports.text:
CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison: chest radiograph 12/29/2025.
Lungs: solitary 2.5 cm nodule in the periphery of the right lower lobe with spiculated margins. No other pulmonary nodule. Airways patent.
Mediastinum and hila: no lymphadenopathy.
Pleura: no effusion.
Heart and great vessels normal.
Upper abdomen: nodular liver contour and splenomegaly, known cirrhosis.
reports.conclusion: Solitary spiculated 2.5 cm peripheral right lower lobe nodule, suspicious for primary lung cancer. No lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion.

reports.text:
Specimen: right lower lobe lung nodule, CT-guided core needle biopsy, 3 cores.
Microscopic: infiltrating glandular neoplasm. Immunohistochemistry: TTF-1 positive.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of lung. Tissue retained for molecular testing.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Pulmonology
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, pulmonary medicine service
Admitted 12/30/2025 (direct admission from primary care), discharged 01/02/2026

Reason for admission: 3-month persistent cough and unintentional 10-lb weight loss with a right lower lobe mass on chest radiograph.

Background: cirrhosis from hepatitis C (cured 2024) with esophageal varices (bled July 2025, banded to eradication), mixed cryoglobulinemia, isoniazid liver injury 2024, resected pheochromocytoma, lichen planus, oral leukoplakia, hypertension. Never smoker, no secondhand smoke exposure. Maternal aunt with lung cancer.

Medications on admission: propranolol 20 mg BID, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, BP 130/85, HR 78, RR 16. Decreased breath sounds over the right lower lobe; no wheezes, rales or rhonchi.

Course: CT chest showed a solitary 2.5 cm spiculated peripheral right lower lobe nodule without lymphadenopathy or effusion. CT-guided core biopsy 12/31 after platelet and INR check, without complication. Pathology: adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive.

Diagnosis: non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe.

Plan: outpatient PET-CT and MRI brain for staging (scheduled 01/06 and 01/07); thoracic surgery consultation 01/08. Molecular testing sent on the biopsy. Discharge medications unchanged.

reports.text: MRI brain, staging for lung adenocarcinoma, performed with and without gadolinium. No enhancing lesion. No mass effect, hemorrhage or acute infarct. Ventricles and sulci normal for age.

documents.title: PET-CT Report
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, nuclear medicine
PET-CT skull base to mid-thigh, 01/06/2026
Indication: staging, right lower lobe adenocarcinoma.
Findings: FDG-avid 2.5 cm right lower lobe nodule, SUVmax 7.8. No FDG-avid hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes. No FDG-avid pleural, osseous, adrenal or hepatic lesion. Cirrhotic liver morphology with splenomegaly, without focal uptake.
Impression: FDG-avid right lower lobe primary. No nodal or distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Consultation
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, thoracic surgery
Date of visit: 01/08/2026

Ms. Lambert, 53, never smoker, has a 2.5 cm biopsy-proven adenocarcinoma in the periphery of the right lower lobe. CT: no adenopathy. PET-CT 01/06: avid primary only. MRI brain 01/07: negative. Clinical stage IA3 (cT1c N0 M0).

Comorbidity: cirrhosis from hepatitis C, decompensated in July with variceal bleeding and ascites, since recompensating on diuretics; varices eradicated 11/19/2025. Recent labs: bilirubin 1.9, albumin 3.2, INR 1.3, platelets 92K. Child-Pugh B7. Reviewed with her gastroenterologist, who supports surgery at this point with close attention to fluid and ascites.

Plan: VATS right lower lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection, 01/15/2026. Risks including bleeding, air leak, pneumonia, liver decompensation, blood clots and death discussed; she wishes to proceed.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, no more than 4 tablets a day

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Thoracic Surgery
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, thoracic surgery
Admitted 01/15/2026, discharged 01/19/2026

Procedure 01/15: VATS right lower lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection.

Course: chest tube removed postoperative day 3. Pain controlled. Diuretics resumed postoperative day 1. Walking in the halls with assistance at discharge; tired and spending most of the day resting.

Final pathology pending at discharge; will be sent to you.

Discharge medications: propranolol 20 mg BID, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily; acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed, maximum 2 g/day.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: thoracic surgery clinic in 2 weeks; oncology once pathology is final.

reports.text:
Specimens: right lower lobe, lobectomy; lymph nodes, stations 4R, 7, 10R, 11R.
Right lower lobe: invasive adenocarcinoma, acinar predominant, 2.5 cm, with a separate 0.8 cm tumor nodule of the same histology in the same lobe. Visceral pleura not involved. Bronchial, vascular and parenchymal margins negative.
Lymph nodes: station 7, 1 of 3 positive; station 4R, 0 of 2; station 10R, 0 of 1; station 11R, 0 of 2.
reports.conclusion: Invasive adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe, 2.5 cm, with separate tumor nodule in the same lobe. Subcarinal node positive. pT3 pN2 (AJCC 8th edition); pathologic stage IIIB with M0.

documents.title: Pathology result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Julie after the lobectomy pathology came in. The surgeon had already gone over it with her this afternoon: a second small tumor in the same lobe and one lymph node under the airway with cancer, so stage IIIB instead of the early stage expected. Margins clear. Oncology is next. She's at home, sore, mostly resting on the couch, walking to the kitchen and bathroom. Encouraged short walks every couple of hours. She asked whether this changes her liver plan; told her no, same meds. Will see her after the oncology visit.

conditions.label: Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale

medications.drug_text: 0.6 ML enoxaparin sodium 100 MG/ML Prefilled Syringe
medications.sig: Inject 60 mg under the skin every 12 hours

reports.text: CT pulmonary angiogram. Acute filling defects in segmental arteries of the left lower lobe. Main and lobar pulmonary arteries patent. RV/LV ratio normal; no right heart strain. Expected postsurgical changes of right lower lobectomy with small right pleural thickening and staple line. No consolidation.
reports.conclusion: Acute segmental pulmonary emboli, left lower lobe, without right heart strain.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 110. Normal axis and intervals. No ST-T changes.
Portable AP chest. Postoperative change of right lower lobectomy with surgical staples. No pneumothorax. No consolidation or significant effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: No acute process. Expected post-lobectomy appearance.

documents.title: ED and Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital
ED arrival 01/25/2026 10:52; admitted to medicine; discharged 01/28/2026

Presentation: 53-year-old woman with stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer, 10 days after VATS right lower lobectomy (01/15), largely bedbound since surgery, with 2 hours of sudden shortness of breath and sharp chest pain worse with deep breaths, plus a mild cough bringing up scant blood-tinged sputum. Also: cirrhosis from hepatitis C with eradicated varices, mixed cryoglobulinemia, resected pheochromocytoma, hypertension.

ED exam: anxious. RR 28, HR 110, BP 130/85, SpO2 89% on room air. Decreased breath sounds at the right base without wheezes or crackles. Remainder unremarkable.

ED data: arterial blood gas on room air pH 7.48, PaCO2 30, PaO2 70, HCO3 24. D-dimer elevated. Troponin and BNP normal. ECG sinus tachycardia. Chest film: no acute process, expected post-lobectomy change. CT pulmonary angiogram: acute segmental emboli in the left lower lobe, no right heart strain.

Course: oxygen by nasal cannula briefly, weaned to room air by day 2. Anticoagulation with enoxaparin 1 mg/kg (60 mg) every 12 hours; low-molecular-weight heparin chosen over oral agents given cirrhosis and active cancer. Platelets 90s. No bleeding. Discharge SpO2 95% on room air.

Diagnosis: acute pulmonary embolism, postoperative.

Discharge medications: enoxaparin 60 mg subcutaneously every 12 hours (new); propranolol 20 mg BID; spironolactone 100 mg daily; furosemide 40 mg daily; acetaminophen as needed, max 2 g/day.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with CBC; oncology as scheduled. Duration of anticoagulation per oncology, at least 6 months.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge after PE (1/25-1/28), 18 days after right lower lobectomy. Turned 54 last week.

Breathing much better. Using acetaminophen once or twice a day for the incisions. No more blood in the sputum. Doing the enoxaparin shots herself into the belly twice a day, no bleeding. No black stools. Oncology appointment 2/11.

Meds: enoxaparin 60 mg q12h, propranolol 20 BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, acetaminophen PRN (max 2 g/day). NKDA.

Exam: BP 118/74, sat as charted on room air. Port sites healing well. Breath sounds reduced at the right base, left clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no fluid wave. Calves soft, nontender, no edema.

A/P
1. Pulmonary embolism: on enoxaparin; CBC today for platelets.
2. Stage IIIB lung adenocarcinoma s/p lobectomy: oncology 2/11.
3. Cirrhosis: labs today. She's due for liver cancer surveillance; ordered ultrasound and AFP for March once she's moving better.
4. Varices eradicated: surveillance EGD in May; continue propranolol.
Med rec complete. See her in 2-3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Monday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Julie, platelets are 95,000, the same range as before surgery and safe on enoxaparin. Hemoglobin 11.0, a little lower after surgery and should recover. Bilirubin 1.7, albumin 3.1, INR 1.3: the liver came through the surgery and the clot without losing ground. Kidney function and potassium fine.

documents.title: RE: Monday's labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good to hear something going right. The pharmacy says my insurance only covers a 30-day supply of the shots at a time, is that something you can change?

documents.title: RE: Monday's labs
documents.author: RN
documents.body: That's a plan limit, not a prescription issue, so 30 days at a time it is. The hospital's prescription has refills on it. We'll make sure oncology takes it over at your 2/11 visit.

documents.title: Molecular Pathology Report
documents.author: pathology
documents.body:
Reference molecular laboratory
Report date: 02/03/2026
Specimen: lung adenocarcinoma, right lower lobe (biopsy 12/31/2025, confirmed on lobectomy).
Method: next-generation sequencing DNA panel; ALK immunohistochemistry.
Results: EGFR exon 19 deletion DETECTED. ALK: negative.
Interpretation: EGFR-sensitizing mutation present.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center, thoracic oncology
Date of visit: 02/11/2026

Ms. Lambert, 54, never smoker, underwent VATS right lower lobectomy on 01/15/2026 for adenocarcinoma: 2.5 cm with a separate same-lobe nodule and one positive subcarinal node, pT3 pN2 M0, stage IIIB. Margins negative. EGFR exon 19 deletion; ALK negative. Postoperative PE on 01/25, on enoxaparin.

Comorbidity: hepatitis C cirrhosis, Child-Pugh B7, eradicated varices, platelets in the 90s. Mixed cryoglobulinemia. NKDA.

Exam: ECOG 1. Healing port sites. Lungs with reduced breath sounds at the right base.

Discussion: adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy is not being offered given her cirrhosis and low platelets. With an EGFR exon 19 deletion, adjuvant osimertinib is recommended; plan 3 years if tolerated. Baseline echocardiogram and ECG before starting.

Plan:
1. Echo and ECG this month; start osimertinib 80 mg daily once reviewed.
2. CBC and liver tests monthly for the first three months, then every 3 months; may be drawn with primary care.
3. Enoxaparin 60 mg every 12 hours; we will prescribe it from here on. Duration at least 6 months and while on cancer treatment.
4. CT chest every 6 months.

Thoracic oncology

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 60% by biplane. Normal diastolic function. Normal right ventricular size and function. No significant valvular disease. Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure normal. No pericardial effusion.
Normal sinus rhythm, rate 64. Normal axis. PR, QRS and QTc intervals normal.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Start
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center, thoracic oncology

Echo 02/23: LVEF 60%. ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal QTc. Specialty pharmacy authorization approved.

Ms. Lambert started adjuvant osimertinib 80 mg by mouth daily on 03/02/2026. Teaching completed with our oncology pharmacist. Enoxaparin continues, now prescribed by our clinic.

Current medications: osimertinib 80 mg daily; enoxaparin 60 mg SC every 12 hours; propranolol 20 mg BID; spironolactone 100 mg daily; furosemide 40 mg daily; acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.

Next: CBC and liver panel in 4 weeks; clinic visit early April.

reports.text: Surveillance abdominal ultrasound. Liver with nodular contour and coarse echotexture; no focal lesion. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. No biliary dilation; gallbladder surgically absent. Spleen 15 cm. Trace perihepatic ascites. Kidneys normal.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhosis with splenomegaly and trace ascites. No focal liver lesion. LI-RADS US-1, negative.

documents.title: Ultrasound and AFP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Surveillance US negative for liver lesion, trace ascites, spleen stable. AFP 4.1, normal. Next due September. Copy to GI.

documents.title: Liver ultrasound
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Julie, yesterday's liver ultrasound shows no spots or masses in the liver, and the AFP blood test is normal. Only a trace of fluid around the liver, less than last summer. We repeat this every six months, next in September.

documents.title: RE: Liver ultrasound
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, I needed one boring result this year. First week on the new cancer pill is done.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center, thoracic oncology
Date of visit: 04/06/2026

Five weeks into adjuvant osimertinib 80 mg daily after resection of stage IIIB EGFR-mutated adenocarcinoma. Tolerating treatment. On enoxaparin for January PE without bleeding.

Labs 04/06: CBC and liver panel stable compared with February.

Plan: continue osimertinib and enoxaparin. CBC and liver panel every 4 weeks through May, then every 3 months; primary care draws are fine. CT chest in June. Return in 10 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, 3 months after lobectomy and PE.

Back at work three days a week from home. Stairs easier, walks around the block most days. On osimertinib since 3/2, oncology says she's tolerating it. Enoxaparin twice a day. No bleeding, no black stools. Weight holding 63. Ascites hasn't come back. No confusion.

Meds: osimertinib 80 daily, enoxaparin 60 q12h, propranolol 20 BID, spironolactone 100, furosemide 40, acetaminophen PRN.

Exam: BP and pulse as charted. Not icteric. Lungs: reduced breath sounds right base, otherwise clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no fluid wave. No edema.

A/P
1. Cirrhosis: labs today, copied to oncology for their monthly monitoring.
2. Lung cancer on adjuvant osimertinib: per oncology.
3. PE: enoxaparin per oncology.
4. Varices: surveillance EGD 5/20.
5. HTN: controlled on propranolol and diuretics.
RTC 3 months.

Addendum: Hgb 11.9, plt 98K; AST 76, ALT 52, bilirubin 1.6, albumin 3.3, INR 1.2. Stable to better. Results sent to oncology.

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology endoscopy unit
Date of procedure: 05/20/2026
Indication: surveillance after eradication of esophageal varices.
Medications reviewed: enoxaparin dose held the evening before and the morning of the procedure per protocol; osimertinib; propranolol; spironolactone; furosemide.
Findings: no recurrent esophageal varices; band scars in the distal esophagus. Stomach and duodenum normal.
Impression: no recurrence.
Plan: resume enoxaparin this evening. Surveillance EGD in 12 months. Continue propranolol.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice
Date of service: 06/15/2026

Yearly oral examination for benign leukoplakia. A hard year: variceal bleeding with cirrhosis from her old hepatitis C last July, then a right lower lobe lung adenocarcinoma resected in January and a pulmonary embolism after surgery. Now on adjuvant osimertinib. Mouth comfortable.

Medications: osimertinib 80 mg daily; enoxaparin 60 mg SC every 12 hours; propranolol 20 mg BID; spironolactone 100 mg daily; furosemide 40 mg daily; acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.

Exam: both buccal mucosae with the white, net-like plaques, unchanged; no new, thickened, red or ulcerated area. Tongue, floor of mouth and gums normal. Wrists with faint brown marks, no active papules.

Assessment: benign oral leukoplakia, stable. Lichen planus, quiet.

Plan: oral examination yearly, next June 2027; sooner for any new, thickening, red or non-healing area.

Dermatology

reports.text:
CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison: 12/30/2025 and CT pulmonary angiogram 01/25/2026.
Postsurgical change of right lower lobectomy with staple line; no nodularity at the resection margin. No new pulmonary nodule. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion. Visualized upper abdomen: cirrhotic liver and splenomegaly, unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Postsurgical change of right lower lobectomy. No evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center, thoracic oncology
Date of visit: 06/24/2026

Nearly 4 months of adjuvant osimertinib 80 mg daily for resected stage IIIB EGFR exon 19-deleted adenocarcinoma. Tolerating it. Enoxaparin continuing for the January PE, no bleeding.

CT chest 06/22: no recurrence. Counts and liver tests stable on the April primary care draw and our May draw.

Plan: continue osimertinib. Continue enoxaparin while on active treatment; will revisit at 6 months on anticoagulation. Labs every 3 months, primary care draw acceptable. Next CT chest December. Return in 3 months.
